title: Minimum Cost of Buying Candies With Discount
summary: A store offers a discount: for every two candies purchased, a third candy is given for free.
statement: A store offers a discount: for every two candies purchased, a third candy is given for free. The customer can select a free candy whose cost does not exceed the minimum cost of the two purchased candies. Given an array of candy costs, calculate the least total cost to buy all candies.
constraints: For every two paid candies, one candy costing no more than either paid candy may be free.
Return the minimum total paid cost to obtain all candies.
hints: To maximize the free discount, sort descending and group each two expensive paid candies with the next cheaper candy.
In descending order, every third candy can legally be free and choosing any cheaper one instead cannot save more.
Sum values whose sorted index modulo three is not two.
An exchange argument pairs each free candy with the nearest two preceding paid costs, maximizing every free contribution without violating its price limit.
editorial: An exchange argument pairs each free candy with the nearest two preceding paid costs, maximizing every free contribution without violating its price limit.

tests.explanation: Pay for costs three and two and receive cost one free, totaling five.
Sorted groups let costs five and two be free, so the minimum paid total is twenty-three.
